t: This is Gower Street in Bloomsbury, running south from Euston Road toward Montague Place, where it becomes Bloomsbury Street. The name comes from Gertrude Leveson-Gower, who married the Duke of Bedford in 1737. Several notable people died on this street. Millicent Garrett Fawcett, who led the National Union of Women's Suffrage Societies from 1897 to 1919 and co-founded Newnham College, Cambridge, died here. So did her sister Agnes Garrett, a suffragist and interior designer. Hensleigh Wedgwood, who wrote a dictionary of English etymology and was a cousin of Charles Darwin, died here too.
